# 1 Maccabees Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_001_page_001.jpg

---

1. And it came to pass after Alexander son of Philip the Macedonian, who came out from the land of Kittim, had struck Darius king of the Persians and the Medes — he reigned in his place, having first reigned over Greece —
2. that he waged many wars and captured strongholds and slew kings of the earth,
3. and went through to the ends of the earth and took plunder from many nations; and the earth fell silent before him, and his heart was lifted up and exalted.
4. And he gathered an exceedingly strong force and ruled over lands and nations and dominions, and they became tributary to him.
5. And after these things he fell upon his bed and knew that he was dying.
6. And he called his servants, the nobles who had been brought up with him from his youth, and he divided his kingdom to them while he was still living.
7. And Alexander reigned twelve years, and he died.
8. And his servants bore rule, each in his own place.
9. And they all put on crowns after his death, and their sons after them for many years, and they multiplied evils upon the earth.
10. And there came forth from them a sinful root — Antiochus Epiphanes, son of Antiochus the king, who had been a hostage at Rome — and he reigned in the one hundred and thirty-seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks.
11. In those days there went out from Israel lawless men, and they persuaded many, saying, "Let us go and make a covenant with the nations that are around us, for since we separated from them many evils have found us."
12. And the word was good in their eyes.
13. And some of the people eagerly went to the king, and he gave them authority to do the ordinances of the nations.
14. And they built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to the custom of the nations,
15. and made themselves foreskins, and departed from the holy covenant, and joined themselves to the nations, and sold themselves to do evil.
16. And the kingdom was established before Antiochus, and he purposed to reign over Egypt, that he might have dominion over two kingdoms.
17. And he entered into Egypt with a strong force, with chariots and with elephants and with horsemen and with a great fleet,
18. and he waged war against Ptolemy king of Egypt; and Ptolemy turned in flight before him, and many fell wounded.
19. And they captured the fortified cities of Egypt, and he took the spoils of Egypt.
20. And Antiochus turned back after he had struck Egypt, in the one hundred and forty-third year, and went up against Israel and against Jerusalem with a strong force.
21. And he entered the sanctuary in arrogance, and took the golden altar and the lampstand of light and all its vessels,
22. and the table of the showbread and the pouring vessels and the cups and the golden censers and the veil and the crowns, and the golden decoration on the face of the temple — he stripped all of it off.
23. And he took the silver and the gold and the precious vessels, and he took the hidden treasures wherever he found them.
24. And he took all and departed to his own land, having made a great slaughter and having spoken in great arrogance.
25. And there was great mourning in Israel, in every place.
26. The rulers and the elders groaned; the virgins and young men languished; the beauty of the women was altered.
27. Every bridegroom took up lamentation; she who sat in the bridal chamber was in mourning.
28. And the land trembled on behalf of its inhabitants, and all the house of Jacob was clothed with shame.
29. And after two years of days the king sent a chief tribute-collector into the cities of Judah, and he came to Jerusalem with a great force.
30. And he spoke to them words of peace in deceit, and they trusted him; and he fell upon the city suddenly and struck it with a great blow, and destroyed many people from Israel.
31. And he spoiled the city and burned it with fire, and tore down its houses and its walls on every side.
32. And they led captive the women and the children, and they seized the cattle.
33. And they built up the city of David with a great and strong wall, with strong towers, and it became for them a citadel.
34. And they placed there a sinful nation, lawless men, and they were strengthened in it.
35. And they stored there weapons and provisions, and gathered the spoils of Jerusalem, and laid them up there, and they became a great snare.
36. And it became a lying-in-wait against the sanctuary, and an evil adversary to Israel continually.
37. And they shed innocent blood around the sanctuary, and defiled the sanctuary.
38. And the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled because of them, and she became a dwelling of strangers; she became strange to her own offspring, and her children forsook her.
39. Her sanctuary was laid waste like a wilderness; her feasts were turned into mourning, her sabbaths into reproach, her honor into contempt.
40. As her glory had been so great, so was her dishonor made great, and her exaltation was turned into mourning.
41. And the king wrote to his whole kingdom that all should become one people,
42. and that each should forsake his own customs.
43. And all the nations submitted according to the word of the king, and many from Israel consented to his worship and sacrificed to the idols and profaned the sabbath.
44. And the king sent letters by the hand of messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, to follow customs that were strange to the land,
45. to prohibit burnt offerings and sacrifice and drink offerings in the sanctuary, and to profane sabbaths and feasts,
46. and to defile the sanctuary and the holy people,
47. to build altars and sacred precincts and shrines for idols, and to sacrifice pigs and unclean animals,
48. and to leave their sons uncircumcised, and to defile their souls with every unclean and profane thing,
49. so that they might forget the Torah and change all the ordinances.
50. And whoever should not act according to the word of the king, he would die.
51. According to all these words he wrote to his whole kingdom, and he appointed overseers over all the people, and he commanded the cities of Judah to sacrifice, city by city.
52. And many from the people gathered to them, everyone who had forsaken the Torah, and they did evil in the land.
53. And they drove Israel into hiding in every place of refuge they had.
54. And on the fifteenth day of Chislev, in the one hundred and forty-fifth year, they set up a desolating abomination upon the altar of burnt offerings, and in the cities of Judah all around they built altars,
55. and at the doors of the houses and in the streets they burned incense.
56. And the scrolls of the Torah which they found they tore in pieces and burned with fire.
57. And wherever a scroll of the covenant was found with any man, and if anyone consented to the Torah, the king's decree sentenced him to death.
58. In their might they acted against Israel, against those who were found month by month in the cities.
59. And on the twenty-fifth of the month they sacrificed upon the altar that was over against the altar of burnt offerings.
60. And the women who had circumcised their children they put to death according to the decree,
61. hanging the infants around their necks, and they put to death also the members of their households and those who had performed the circumcision.
62. And many in Israel stood firm and were strengthened in themselves not to eat unclean food.
63. And they chose to die rather than to be defiled by food or to profane the holy covenant, and they died.
64. And very great wrath came upon Israel.
